- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

20	// ExtractedData contains all metadata extracted from markdown in a single pass.
21	type ExtractedData struct {

25	}

27	// Service handles markdown metadata extraction.

29	// HTML rendering is primarily done on frontend using markdown-it, but backend provides
30	// RenderHTML for RSS feeds and other server-side rendering needs.
31	type Service interface {
32		// ExtractAll extracts tags, properties, and references in a single parse (most efficient)
33		ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)
34	
35		// ExtractTags returns all #tags found in content
36		ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)
37	
38		// ExtractProperties computes boolean properties
39		ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)
40

42		RenderMarkdown(content []byte) (string, error)

45		RenderHTML(content []byte) (string, error)
46

49

51		ValidateContent(content []byte) error
52	
53		// RenameTag renames all occurrences of oldTag to newTag in content
54		RenameTag(content []byte, oldTag, newTag string) (string, error)
55	}
56	
57	// service implements the Service interface.
58	type service struct {
59		md goldmark.Markdown
60	}
61	
62	// Option configures the markdown service.
63	type Option func(*config)
64	
65	type config struct {
66		enableTags     bool
67		enableMentions bool
68	}
69	
70	// WithTagExtension enables #tag parsing.
71	func WithTagExtension() Option {
72		return func(c *config) {
73			c.enableTags = true
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// WithMentionExtension enables @mention parsing.
78	func WithMentionExtension() Option {
79		return func(c *config) {
80			c.enableMentions = true
81		}
82	}
83	
84	// NewService creates a new markdown service with the given options.
85	func NewService(opts ...Option) Service {
86		cfg := &config{}
87		for _, opt := range opts {
88			opt(cfg)
89		}
90	
91		exts := []goldmark.Extender{
92			extension.GFM, // GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks)
93		}
94	
95		// Add custom extensions based on config
96		if cfg.enableTags {
97			exts = append(exts, extensions.TagExtension)
98		}
99		if cfg.enableMentions {
100			exts = append(exts, extensions.MentionExtension)
101		}
102	
103		md := goldmark.New(
104			goldmark.WithExtensions(exts...),
105			goldmark.WithParserOptions(
106				parser.WithAutoHeadingID(), // Generate heading IDs
107			),
108		)
109	
110		return &service{

112		}
113	}

117		reader := text.NewReader(content)
118		doc := s.md.Parser().Parse(reader)
119		return doc, nil
120	}

h14.

**Computation site:** `RebuildMemoPayload()` in `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88`, which delegates the actual parsing to `(*service).ExtractAll()` in `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:355-413` (a single goldmark AST walk). The results are written into `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (a `storepb.MemoPayload_Property`, defined in `proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go`).

**Triggers (recomputation runs whenever memo content changes or is backfilled):**
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, called on every new memo before it's persisted.
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, called only when the update mask includes the `content` path (i.e., the memo body itself was edited); other field updates (visibility, pinned, state, etc.) don't trigger it.
- Bulk backfill/migration — `Runner.RunOnce()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72`, a maintenance job that pages through all memos in batches of 100 and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` + `Store.UpdateMemo` on each, rebuilding payloads for existing data (e.g., after a schema/logic change).

**Extracted properties** (from `ExtractedData` in `markdown.go:20-25` and the `Property` struct fields set during the walk):
- `Tags` — all `#tag` nodes found via the custom tag extension, deduplicated case-preservingly (`data.Tags = uniquePreserveCase(data.Tags)`).
- `Property.Title` — text of the first block-level child if it's an H1 heading.
- `Property.HasLink` — true if any Markdown link node is present.
- `Property.HasCode` — true if any code block, fenced code block, or code span is present.
- `Property.HasTaskList` — true if any GFM task checkbox is present.
- `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any task checkbox is unchecked.
- (`Mentions` is also extracted in the same pass but is not stored on `Payload`; it's used elsewhere, e.g. for mention notifications, not for the persisted list/preview metadata.)

## 1. Where the computation happens

**Core extraction logic (goldmark AST parsing):** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`
- `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` — lines 356-422. Single-pass extraction of tags, mentions, and properties.
- `ExtractProperties(content []byte)` — lines 192-241 (equivalent single-purpose function).

- `RenameTag` — lines 424-453 (rewrites tags in content, used for tag-rename operations, not derivation per se).

**Orchestration / "on save" hook:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`
- `RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` — lines 74-88. Calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(memo.Content)` and writes the result into `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`.
- `Runner.RunOnce` — lines 26-72: a batch job that reloads all memos and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` on each, then persists via `Store.UpdateMemo`. Note: this `Runner`/`RunOnce` is **not currently wired up** in `/bench/repo/server/server.go`'s `startBackgroundRunners` (only the `s3presign` runner is started there) — so today it exists as backfill/migration infrastructure but isn't invoked automatically anywhere in the traced code.

**List/preview snippet generation (separate from Payload, computed on every read/convert):** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, lines 83-90:
```go
func (s *APIV1Service) getMemoContentSnippet(content string) (string, error) {
    snippet, err := s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)
    ...
}
```
Used in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` line 76-80 (`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`), lines 221-273 (memo relations list), `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` lines 318-391 (notification snippets for comment/mention events), and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` lines 154-173.

## 2. What triggers recomputation

- **CreateMemo** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108): `RebuildMemoPayload` is called on every new memo before it's persisted.
- **UpdateMemo, only when `content` is in the update mask** (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` lines 435-451): when `path == "content"`, the handler sets `memo.Content` then calls `RebuildMemoPayload` again, storing the new `Payload` alongside the new content. Other update paths (visibility, pinned, state, location, etc.) do NOT trigger recomputation.
- **Snippet (`getMemoContentSnippet`)** is computed on-the-fly every time a memo is converted to its API representation (list responses, relation previews, notification payloads) — it is not persisted in `Payload`, unlike tags/properties/title.
- **Batch backfill** via `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — iterates all memos and rebuilds payloads; present in code but not currently scheduled/called from `server.go` (dead/unused wiring at present, likely intended as a one-off migration tool).

## 3. Exact fields extracted/computed

From `ExtractAll`/`ExtractProperties` (stored persistently in `store.Memo.Payload`, proto `storepb.MemoPayload`):
- **Tags**: `[]string` — parsed from `#tag` AST nodes (goldmark `TagExtension`), excluding tags inside links/images, deduplicated preserving original case. (`markdown.go` lines 142-170, 376-378, 418)
- **Property.Title**: `string` — extracted only when the *first block-level child of the document* is an H1 heading; plain text content of that heading. (`markdown.go` lines 207-213, 383-389)
- **Property.HasLink**: `bool` — true if any `gast.KindLink` node exists. (lines 216-217, 393-394)
- **Property.HasCode**: `bool` — true if any code block, fenced code block, or code span exists. (lines 219-220, 396-397)
- **Property.HasTaskList**: `bool` — true if any GFM task checkbox exists. (lines 222-223, 399-400)
- **Property.HasIncompleteTasks**: `bool` — true if any task checkbox is unchecked. (lines 224-228, 401-405)
- **Mentions**: `[]string` — `@mention` usernames (lowercased, deduplicated) extracted via `MentionExtension`, though not persisted into `MemoPayload` (used elsewhere for notifications, not part of `RebuildMemoPayload`'s writes — only `Tags` and `Property` are assigned in `runner.go` lines 85-86).

From `GenerateSnippet` (computed transiently for API responses, not persisted):
- **Snippet**: plain-text preview, max length 64 chars (per `getMemoContentSnippet`), built by walking the AST and concatenating text nodes/autolink URLs/`#tag` text while skipping code blocks, inserting spaces between block elements, then truncated at the last word boundary within the max length with `" ..."` appended if truncated.

Not present anywhere in the codebase: word count, reading time — I searched for `wordCount`, `readingTime`, `word_count`, `reading_time` across both the Go backend and the `web/` frontend and found no matches, so those fields simply aren't computed/derived for memos in this repo.</result>
